result.topic_en: Euler finishes a numerical example comparing the height to which water rises through a tube inclined at half a right angle with the preceding case, then begins Case V: water flowing from a vessel through an inclined or bent tube and out through a vertical tube.

der tubum, angulo ſemirecto, ad horizontem inclinatum, ad eundem locum C deduci, eſſeque vt ante $gg=\frac{1}{100}$, ſeu $g=\frac{1}{10}$ ped. erit coſ. $\zeta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ et $b=100\sqrt{2}$ $=14,14$ ped.

95. Cum igitur ſit $\frac{ab}{g}=0,3536$, erit $\mathfrak{B}=0,7021$. Statuamus, vt ibi orificium $kk$ minimum, et ob $a$ quantitatem minimam, erit
$$v=0,2979\left(\frac{100}{\sqrt{2}}-30\right)=75,309 \text{ pedum.}$$
Quae quantitas cum ſit maior, quam caſu praecedente, $5\frac{2}{3}$ pedibus, ſequitur aquam hoc caſu ad altitudinem maiorem eſſe aſcenſuram, quam caſu praecedente.

CASVS V.

SI AQVA EX VASE $AB$ VEL PER TVBVM CYLINDRICVM INCLINATVM $BE$, VEL PER INFLEXVM $bcE$ DEFLVAT ET INDE PER TVBVM VERTICALEM $CD$ ERVMPAT.

96. Sit vaſis AB altitudo $a$ minima, amplitudo vero $ff$ maxima: tum, quia hic duos caſus euoluere conſtitui, ſit pro vtroque caſu amplitudo tubi deferentis $BB=bb=cc=gg$, tubuli verticalis CD altitudo $=c$, et amplitudo $CC=bb$, et lumen in $DD=kk$. Tum pro caſu priori ſit longitudo tubi $BE=b$, eiusque ad verticalem inclinatio $=\zeta$; erit pro caſu altero $bc=b\,\text{coſ.}\,\zeta$, et $cE=b\,\text{ſin.}\,\zeta$. Ponatur autem $\frac{k^4}{g^4}=\mathfrak{G}$ et $\frac{k^4}{b^4}=\mathfrak{H}$.

67. His

items.english: Since this quantity is greater by 5 2/3 feet than in the preceding case, it follows that the water in this case will rise to a greater height than in the preceding case.
